description: Realistic full-stack integration prompts that should trigger and exercise the quo (formerly OpenPhone) skill. Use with skill-evaluator / the skill-creator eval loop to benchmark with-skill vs baseline.

evals.name: send-sms-nextjs-server-route
evals.prompt: I'm building a Next.js app and want to text customers an order confirmation from my OpenPhone number when they check out. Wire up a server route that sends the SMS so my API key never hits the browser. My sending number is +14155550100.
evals.expected_output: Sends via POST https://api.quo.com/v1/messages from a SERVER-side route (App Router route handler / API route), with Authorization set to the RAW key (NO 'Bearer'), body { from, to: [E.164], content }. Notes that 'to' is exactly one E.164 recipient, content is 1-1600 chars, and the call returns 202 Accepted (queued) — delivery is async, confirmed via a message.delivered webhook or GET /v1/messages/{id}. Mentions US A2P 10DLC registration is required to send to US numbers. May use scripts/quo-client.mjs or scaffold-quo.mjs.

evals.name: verified-webhook-receiver-express
evals.prompt: Add a webhook endpoint to my Express server so I get notified when someone texts my Quo number, and make sure nobody can POST fake events to it.
evals.expected_output: Uses the BETA webhook API. Verifies the signature: HMAC-SHA256 base64 over `{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{raw-body}` using the whsec_-prefixed signing secret (stripped + base64-decoded), comparing against the space-separated `v1,<sig>` entries in the webhook-signature header, with a ~5-min timestamp tolerance. Captures the RAW body (express.raw) BEFORE JSON parsing, de-duplicates on the webhook-id HEADER (not envelope id), and handles message.received. Ideally uses scripts/verify-webhook.js. Notes the secret is returned only at create/rotate time.

evals.name: two-way-sms-autoreply
evals.prompt: I want an SMS auto-responder with OpenPhone: when a customer texts our support line, automatically reply with a confirmation that we got their message. Full loop please.
evals.expected_output: Combines a verified beta webhook receiver (message.received) with a send call (POST /v1/messages). Reads the inbound text from event.data.resource.text and the sender from event.data.context (senderIdentifier / phoneNumberId), then replies with `from` = the Quo number and `to` = the sender. Stresses webhook signature verification, idempotency on webhook-id (so retries don't double-reply), acking 200 fast, the 10 req/s rate limit, and 202-async send semantics. Flags A2P registration for US.

evals.name: 401-auth-bearer-debug
evals.prompt: My OpenPhone API calls keep returning 401 Unauthorized. I'm setting the header to `Authorization: Bearer op_live_xxx` and hitting https://api.openphone.com/v1/phone-numbers. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Identifies the root cause: Quo/OpenPhone does NOT use a Bearer token — the Authorization header must be the RAW API key alone (`Authorization: op_live_xxx`), no 'Bearer ' prefix. Confirms api.openphone.com/v1 is a valid (alias) host (api.quo.com/v1 is canonical), so the host isn't the problem. May mention the key must be generated by a workspace owner/admin and that the live error body is {error:{message,key,trace}}.

evals.name: call-transcripts-and-contacts-crm
evals.prompt: We want to pull every call's AI summary and transcript into our CRM, and create/update a contact for each external caller. Walk me through the Quo endpoints and the gotchas.
evals.expected_output: Uses GET /v1/calls (requires phoneNumberId + participants + maxResults) with pageToken pagination (loop until nextPageToken is null; totalItems is inaccurate), then GET /v1/call-summaries/{callId} and GET /v1/call-transcripts/{id} — noting the transcript path param is `id` not `callId`, that both are business/scale-plan-gated, and that results are async (poll processingStatus until completed). For contacts: POST/PATCH /v1/contacts with the nested defaultFields/customFields shape (firstName required), upsert by externalId. Recommends subscribing to call.summary.completed / call.transcript.completed webhooks instead of polling. Auth is the raw key (no Bearer).

evals.name: tanstack-ai-quo-assistant-tools
evals.prompt: We're on TanStack Start + @tanstack/ai (anthropic adapter). I want an in-app assistant for our support team that can look at our Quo inbox, tell us which customers we haven't replied to, summarize yesterday's missed calls and voicemails, and text customers back. A human has to approve every text before it goes out. Our support line's phone number id is PNsupport01. Build the server tools + the chat route.
evals.expected_output: Server-only TanStack AI tools built with toolDefinition + Zod inputSchema and .server(); send tool has needsApproval: true and calls POST /v1/messages (v1 is the only send surface) with raw-key auth; reads use the 2026-03-30 surface with Quo-Api-Version header (GET /calls with include=summary,voicemail, GET /conversations or /messages); inbox scoped to PNsupport01 and re-checked inside execute; tool errors returned as data; no auto-retry of sends; rate limit 10 req/s respected (shared limiter / sequential tool execution); customer text treated as untrusted; chat route passes resume for approvals.
assertions: Authorization header carries the raw API key with no 'Bearer' prefix

Uses the 2026-03-30 surface (unprefixed path with Quo-Api-Version: 2026-03-30) for at least one read that v1 cannot do as efficiently (workspace-wide calls/messages/conversations), and every such request carries the header
Rate limit of 10 req/s per key is enforced in code (shared limiter, throttle or sequential execution), not just mentioned
SMS is sent via POST /v1/messages (the v1 path)
Send tool is defined with TanStack AI toolDefinition + Zod inputSchema and implemented with .server()
Send tool sets needsApproval: true
Inbox restriction to PNsupport01 is re-checked server-side inside the tool's execute (not only in the prompt)
A send that fails with 5xx/timeout is not automatically retried
Missed calls are fetched with summaries/voicemails inline (include=summary,voicemail or equivalent single list) rather than one extra request per call
Customer-authored text (SMS bodies, transcripts) is treated as untrusted data (labelled, or explicit prompt-injection guard)
Chat route forwards the resume/approval continuation payload to chat()
Multiple recipients in one send are prevented or explicitly warned as a shared group thread
The same approved send cannot execute twice (idempotency ledger keyed by tool call / approval, or a reconciliation lookup before any resend)
Finding unreplied customers and missed calls costs O(pages) Quo requests, not one or more requests per conversation or per call
Missed calls are identified as incoming calls that were never answered, not by a single status value
Approval is bound server-side to the exact recipients/content (and approving actor), not only to a UI click
AI call summaries are returned for yesterday's missed calls when available

evals.name: call-analytics-structured-report
evals.prompt: Every morning I want a job that pulls all of yesterday's calls from our OpenPhone (now Quo) workspace with the AI call summaries and has an LLM produce a structured JSON report: totals, missed calls, top 5 call reasons with example call ids, and a follow-up list. Use TanStack AI. We have ~300 calls a day so don't blow the rate limit.
evals.expected_output: Uses GET /calls on the 2026-03-30 API (Quo-Api-Version header, unprefixed path, createdAt[gte]/[lte] UTC window, include=summary,voicemail, limit=50 + after/nextCursor pagination) instead of N+1 per-call summary fetches; handles summary.status absent/in-progress/failed and Business/Scale plan gating; stays under 10 req/s; uses TanStack AI structured output (chat with outputSchema Zod) to produce the report; raw key auth with no Bearer.
assertions: Authorization header carries the raw API key with no 'Bearer' prefix

Uses the 2026-03-30 surface (unprefixed path with Quo-Api-Version: 2026-03-30) for at least one read that v1 cannot do as efficiently (workspace-wide calls/messages/conversations), and every such request carries the header
Rate limit of 10 req/s per key is enforced in code (shared limiter, throttle or sequential execution), not just mentioned
Uses GET /calls on the 2026-03-30 surface (unprefixed path) with a createdAt[gte]/[lte] UTC window for yesterday
Requests summaries inline with include=summary (no per-call summary request)
Paginates with limit=50 and after/nextCursor until nextCursor is null
Handles summary status other than completed (absent / in-progress / failed) explicitly
Produces the report via TanStack AI structured output (chat with a Zod outputSchema)
Mentions that call summaries require the Business or Scale plan
Fetching ~300 calls costs O(pages) Quo requests (about 6-10), not one request per call or per conversation
Missed calls are identified as incoming calls that were never answered (covers busy/canceled/completed-without-answer), not only status=missed
Missed-call count excludes AI-handled and forwarded calls
The fetch is complete for the workspace (no per-conversation fan-out that skips group calls or unscanned conversations)

evals.name: reminder-scheduling-agent-tool
evals.prompt: our clinic uses Quo for texting. I need appointment reminders sent 24h before each appointment, and our TanStack AI chat assistant should be able to schedule a one-off reminder text when staff ask it to ("remind Jane at 9am tomorrow about her follow-up"). If the patient doesn't reply to confirm, a staff member should get a follow-up task. How do I build this?
evals.expected_output: States Quo has no scheduled-send endpoint; scheduling is an app-side durable job queue whose worker calls POST /v1/messages at send time (no auto-retry; idempotent job, look up before resending); assistant tool to schedule has needsApproval and requires explicit time-zone offset; re-checks consent/opt-out/quiet hours at send time; uses Quo tasks with dueDate (POST /v1/tasks linked to activity/conversation, or 2026-03-30 task endpoints) for staff follow-up and optionally task.overdue / message.received webhooks to detect confirmation.
assertions: Authorization header carries the raw API key with no 'Bearer' prefix

Uses the 2026-03-30 surface (unprefixed path with Quo-Api-Version: 2026-03-30) for at least one read that v1 cannot do as efficiently (workspace-wide calls/messages/conversations), and every such request carries the header
Rate limit of 10 req/s per key is enforced in code (shared limiter, throttle or sequential execution), not just mentioned
States that Quo has no scheduled-send endpoint and scheduling must be app-side
Uses a durable job queue/scheduler whose worker calls POST /v1/messages at the send time
The assistant's schedule-reminder tool requires human approval (needsApproval: true)
Requires or converts to an explicit time-zone offset for the reminder time
Re-checks consent/opt-out (STOP) or quiet hours at send time
Creates a Quo task (with dueDate) for staff follow-up when the patient does not confirm
Detects confirmation replies via a signature-verified message.received webhook
Send in the worker is not auto-retried blindly (idempotent job / look up before resend)
Each reminder send has exactly one recipient (no accidental group thread)
The assistant's scheduling tool takes a patient/contact id resolved server-side, or otherwise prevents the model from texting an arbitrary number
The rate limit holds across processes (shared/injected limiter or an explicit split of the 10 req/s budget between worker and web)
Every Quo request in every process (worker, web, webhook handler) goes through one limiter per process within the 10 req/s per-key budget
Quiet hours are re-checked at send time, not only when scheduling
Any resend-reconciliation lookup uses only filter operators the endpoint defines (GET /messages: createdAt[gt]/[lt])
